weather_report:
Subiaco slips through the small hours under a soft lid of cloud, the streetlights haloed and the night sounding hushed. It feels cool and settled, with no moonlit bite and no starlight, just a calm, even gray above. UV is effectively absent now, and the sky offers little in the way of sparkle; clarity is diffuse rather than crisp, like looking through frosted glass.

Toward dawn the blanket loosens into broken cloud, letting through shy, filtered light. Expect a gentle, matte morning rather than anything gleaming, with the sun hesitant at first and UV staying tame early; if the gaps widen later, brightness will build without turning harsh. It reads as a comfortable, unhurried start: a light layer or long sleeves will suit, maybe a thin jacket if you run cool. This is good weather for ordinary rituals done well—a quiet walk before the traffic stirs, a ride to pick up bread, watering the plants, or setting up at a window with a notebook and a patient cup of coffee as the sky slowly shakes itself awake.
